title: Voice-Enabled Technical Interview Simulation Engine with Asynchronous Speech Processing & Evaluation
problem: Technical mock interview platforms struggle with high speech-to-text latency, conversational interruptions, and subjective, uncalibrated feedback scoring. Relying on synchronous, single-turn LLM calls produces unrealistic dialog pacing and hallucinatory performance rubrics. This project builds an asynchronous voice-enabled interview simulation platform in Python and FastAPI. The engine accepts spoken audio streams, transcribes candidate responses using faster-whisper, evaluates technical depth and behavioral STAR structure using DSPy metric pipelines with LangChain, and returns structured feedback with actionable code corrections across WebSockets.

use_cases.title: Automated Candidate Screenings for Engineering Teams
use_cases.first_sentence: Recruiting teams at high-volume software agencies require consistent initial technical screenings without consuming senior engineering hours.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine conducts automated 15-minute technical question drills, generating structured scoring reports and code diff suggestions for hiring managers.

use_cases.title: Interactive University Career Placement Labs
use_cases.first_sentence: Computer science departments need scalable interview preparation laboratories where graduating students practice algorithmic problem explanation under time constraints.
use_cases.second_sentence: Students verbalize design trade-offs and code logic into browser microphones, receiving immediate latency-calibrated evaluation on communication clarity and algorithmic soundness.

use_cases.title: Corporate Lateral Hiring Preparation Portals
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise internal mobility programs require standardized assessment environments for junior engineers seeking promotion to mid-level engineering tiers.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system runs targeted system design and coding mock interviews, evaluating structural responses against standardized competency rubrics without human bias.

hard_parts: Minimizing audio chunk streaming latency across WebSockets while maintaining Whisper transcription word accuracy
Constructing deterministic, calibrated scoring rubrics with DSPy assertion pipelines that prevent LLM hallucination and grade inflation
Managing conversational state, interruption handling, and turn-taking without race conditions in asynchronous asyncio queues
Synthesizing structured candidate feedback containing precise syntactic corrections and rubric-grounded improvement suggestions
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase separating WebSocket transport, Whisper transcription pipelines, and DSPy evaluation runners
Rigorous speech-to-text benchmark measuring word error rate and transcription latency across diverse synthetic accent datasets
Anti-fake verification script streaming raw audio chunks and verifying real-time WebSocket token dispatch and structured JSON rubric emission

architecture.data_flow: The candidate speaks into the browser microphone; the React frontend captures 16kHz PCM audio frames and streams them over WebSockets to FastAPI; the streaming gateway buffers frames into temporal chunks; the Whisper pipeline transcribes speech into text segments; the dialogue manager appends transcript tokens to the active interview session state; once candidate turn completion is detected, the DSPy evaluation engine runs calibrated scoring pipelines against standardized technical rubrics; structured evaluation JSON and synthesized audio responses stream back over WebSockets to update the React UI.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Strict schema validation using Pydantic models on evaluation output; hard audio buffer bounds preventing memory bloat during candidate speech.

targets.method: Levenshtein distance calculation between Whisper transcribed outputs and verified ground-truth transcripts across audio benchmark
targets.input: 50 synthetic mock interview audio recordings (16kHz WAV format, 2 to 5 minutes duration each, technical terminology)
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, 8GB RAM, Whisper small/base CPU quantization
targets.minimum_pass: Average Word Error Rate across 50 audio recordings is < 12.0%
targets.target: Average Word Error Rate across 50 audio recordings is < 6.5%
targets.report: Whisper ASR accuracy and Word Error Rate evaluation summary report

targets.method: Wall-clock timing from client WebSocket audio chunk dispatch to initial transcription text emission
targets.input: 100 distinct 3-second audio test packets streamed across local loopback WebSocket connection
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Python 3.11 asynchronous runtime
targets.minimum_pass: p95 transcription latency per 3-second chunk is < 850 milliseconds
targets.target: p95 transcription latency per 3-second chunk is < 420 milliseconds
targets.report: WebSocket streaming latency and audio processing timing log

targets.metric: Evaluation Rubric Score Consistency with Human Baseline
targets.method: Pearson correlation coefficient between automated DSPy evaluation scores and calibrated senior interviewer ratings
targets.input: 40 paired candidate interview responses with curated 5-point technical rubric ratings
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, DSPy assertion pipeline with Ollama or local mock LLM
targets.minimum_pass: Pearson correlation coefficient r >= 0.78 across 40 responses
targets.target: Pearson correlation coefficient r >= 0.89 across 40 responses
targets.report: Automated evaluation calibration and human rating correlation matrix

environment.ram: 8GB RAM (16GB recommended for local Whisper medium models)
environment.gpu: None strictly required (quantized faster-whisper CPU inference supported)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source local models via faster-whisper and Ollama)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Python 3.11, faster-whisper CPU release, and modern Chromium browser
environment.fallback_path: Local pre-recorded audio file playback through REST API if browser microphone input is disabled

riskiest_component.name: Whisper CPU Transcription Latency on Continuous Audio Buffers
riskiest_component.mitigation: Utilize faster-whisper with INT8 quantization, 3-second minimum chunk windows, and VAD (Voice Activity Detection) silences.
riskiest_component.fallback: Whisper-tiny model or local wav2vec2 lightweight acoustic model for ultra-low CPU footprint.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an asynchronous voice interview simulation platform in Python/FastAPI with faster-whisper ASR, DSPy evaluation pipelines, and WebSockets.
worksheet.q2: Target users: engineering hiring teams, career development centers, and software engineers practicing technical communication.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: automated candidate pre-screening, university placement laboratories, and internal engineering promotion assessments.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: streaming audio chunk buffering over WebSockets, minimizing Whisper transcription latency on CPU, DSPy assertion calibration, and turn-taking state machines.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 50 synthetic 16kHz WAV recordings, reference transcript manifests, and rubric schemas. Synthetic recordings only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local REST audio file upload.
